newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mortars fired from Lebanon slam into Israel.
newsitem.headline: Mortars fired from Lebanon slam into Israel.

text.p: Several mortars fired from Lebanon slammed into Israel early on Wednesday, Israeli security sources said.
They said it appeared no one was injured. The mortars were probably aimed at Israeli military posts in south Lebanon and overshot their mark, the sources said.
The army said it was checking the report.
It was the second time this week that mortars hit northern Israel after fierce weekend fighting between the Israeli army and Hizbollah guerrillas in southern Lebanon.
Under a U.S.-brokered deal that halted Israel's 17-day blitz of Lebanon in April 1996, Hizbollah is obliged to refrain from firing rockets or mortars into the Jewish state.
The accord, which ended a blitz that killed 200 people, mainly civilians, banned shooting from or at civilian areas in Israel's war in south Lebanon with Hizbollah guerrillas.
Hizbollah guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local militia allies from the 15-km (nine-mile)-wide border zone they hold in south Lebanon.
